strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy/scipy#20405 by running the added regression test `test_yn_gh_20405` that checks `scipy.special.cephes.yn(500, 1)` returns exactly `-np.inf`. On the buggy revision it returns `NaN` (or another non-`-inf`), so the exact comparison fails; on the fixed revision it terminates the Cephes recurrence early and returns `-inf` so the assertion passes. This strategy uses the project’s own test command and does not rely on printing/inspecting values beyond the test assertion.

pinned_because: SciPy’s special functions (Cephes/AMOS translations) are C/Fortran-backed; installing SciPy from source in editable mode ensures the compiled extension corresponds exactly to the target buggy and fixed revisions. Pinning NumPy and building from source are required to make the failure deterministic, but the evidence does not provide a specific NumPy version constraint—so choose a reasonable compatible default and keep it the same across buggy vs fixed runs.

strategy.success_criterion: The test `assert observed == -np.inf` fails on the buggy revision (observed is not `-inf`, observed is `NaN` per the evidence chain for the same recurrence path) and passes on the fixed revision (observed is exactly `-inf`).
risks: The evidence ties the observed failure to a specific recurrence termination change in `scipy/special/cephes/yn.c` (from `while (k < n);` to `while (k < n && isfinite(an));`). If the buggy revision you check out already includes that change (or if a downstream backport exists), the test may pass and you won’t see the regression.

Reproducing the `NaN` behavior for `yv` may depend on the Amos Fortran->C translation path, but this strategy intentionally uses the project’s direct Cephes-level regression (`cephes.yn(500, 1)`) so you don’t need to rely on the higher-level fallback behavior to transition.

Exact equality to `-np.inf` is sensitive to platform/FP behavior; however the regression test uses exact equality in the project, so the environment should match the project’s CI expectations (run on typical x86_64 Linux/macOS with standard floating-point).

If your platform uses different libm/denormal/fast-math flags that alter how the recurrence overflows to `-inf` vs `NaN`, the test could fail even on the fixed revision. The required transition is still the same (test fails on buggy, passes on fixed), but results may vary on nonstandard toolchains/sanitizers.

oracle.why: The regression is specifically about correct asymptotic termination in Cephes `yn` recurrence; the test enforces exact `-inf` as the expected correct result for (n=500, x=1).

fails_on_buggy.description: On the buggy revision, `observed = cephes.yn(500, 1)` evaluates to `NaN` (per the evidence chain: the recurrence continues past overflow, producing `NaN`). Since `NaN != -np.inf`, `assert observed == -np.inf` fails.

passes_on_fixed.description: On the fixed revision, the updated termination condition stops the recurrence when the intermediate `an` becomes infinite (or `-inf`), preventing `NaN` propagation; `observed` becomes exactly `-np.inf`, so `assert observed == -np.inf` passes.
